description: Two-channel oscilloscope, drawing voltage against time or one channel against the other

params.text: Zooms channel 1 vertically, from 20V across the screen down to 0.078V
Moves channel 1 up and down the screen, adding a voltage offset before the zoom
Zooms channel 2 vertically, from 20V across the screen down to 0.078V
Moves channel 2 up and down the screen, adding a voltage offset before the zoom
Sets how much time the screen covers, from 5ms to 50 seconds; in the two-against-each-other mode it sets the sampling rate and the length of the trail
Switches between drawing both signals against time and drawing channel 1 horizontally against channel 2 vertically, which makes a Lissajous figure from two sine waves
Sets the voltage that triggering fires at, marked on the display with a T
Turns on triggering, so drawing starts when channel 1 crosses the threshold and a repeating waveform holds its place on the screen

inputs.text: A signal here starts the drawing instead of channel 1

outputs.text: Channel 1 passed through unchanged, for carrying on to another module
Channel 2 passed through unchanged, for carrying on to another module

notes: the three readouts for each channel are labelled pp, max and min: the peak-to-peak swing, the highest voltage and the lowest voltage across the window on screen
each trace is drawn in the colour of the cable patched into that input, and every channel of a polyphonic cable is drawn
